core_obligations: Reduce to an affine base (proof lines 8363-8375): the question is local on Y, so the author assumes Y affine, and then X and Y' are affine as well because f is integral, which reduces the comparison to rings.

Compare the two sides (proof lines 8375-8395): in the affine case the pushforward is computed by the sections over the base change, and both sides give the same description, which yields the equality.
Conclude (proof lines 8395-8404): the local computation descends to the general case because the assertion is local on Y.
proof_roadmap: Localise on Y and use integrality to make all schemes involved affine.
Compute both pushforwards through the sections over the base change.
Conclude the equality and descend to the general case.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves base change for the pushforward along an integral morphism: for a cartesian square with f integral and any sheaf of sets on X_etale, the pushforward of the pullback equals the pullback of the pushforward (statement lines 8349-8361). The proof localises on Y and uses integrality to reduce to the affine case (proof lines 8363-8375), where both sides are computed through the sections over the base change (proof lines 8375-8395), and then descends the local computation (proof lines 8395-8404). The non-formal content is the affine computation where integrality is used to make the schemes affine. The claim is H2: one reduction plus one affine computation.
